qns_content.text: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">In flowering plants, how many division are required for the formation of mature male gametophyte from microspore mother cell ?<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"Correct Answer:3. One meiotic and Two mitotic
Explanation (NCERT-based): 
In flowering plants, the development of the mature male gametophyte (pollen grain) involves the following steps: 
1. Meiotic Division: 
  • The microspore mother cell (MMC) undergoes meiosis to produce a tetrad of four haploid microspores. 
  • This is a single meiotic division. 
2. First Mitotic Division: 
  • Each haploid microspore undergoes mitosis to form two cells: 
 A vegetative cell (larger, metabolically active). 
 A generative cell (smaller, which later forms gametes). 
3. Second Mitotic Division: 
  • The generative cell undergoes one more mitosis to produce two haploid male gametes, completing the development of the mature male gametophyte.
Summary:
  • Total divisions:
  • One meiotic division (in MMC).
Thus, the correct answer is One meiotic and Two mitotic."

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">Read the given statements and select the correct option.<br \/>\n<strong>Statement 1 :<\/strong> In insertional inactivation

blue colour produced by bacterial colonies indicate that the vector doesn't have the insert (gene of interest)<br \/>\n<strong>Statement 2 :<\/strong> Presence  of insert (gene of interest) results into insertional inactivation of the marker enzyme (β-galactosidase) and colonies do not produce any colour.<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"Statement 1: 
• In insertional inactivation, if a foreign gene is inserted into a vector (such as a plasmid containing a lacZ gene for β-galactosidase), the function of the β-galactosidase enzyme is disrupted. 
• As a result, bacterial colonies that do not have the insert will produce a blue color in the presence of a substrate like X-gal (which is cleaved by β-galactosidase). Therefore, blue colonies indicate the absence of the insert. 
Statement 2: 
• When the insert (gene of interest) is present, it disrupts the lacZ gene (encoding β-galactosidase), causing the colonies to lose their ability to produce the blue color. These colonies will appear white, indicating that the β-galactosidase enzyme is not functional due to insertional inactivation."
